To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Dup is stabilized by replication defects and (2) Gem levels are increased in cells with elevated Dup levels, and that this is important to prevent re-formation of a pre-RC.
Dup destruction is dependent upon DNA replication, not the cell-cycle checkpoint, and that Dup and Gem levels increase in response to defects in DNA replication.

(1) the origin-binding protein Dup is rapidly destroyed at G1-S by cyclin-E/ CDK2; (2) DNA replication triggers the degradation of Dup; (3) Dup stabilization is not dependent upon ATM/ ATR checkpoint kinases and (4) Dup stabilization is sensitive both to the type of cell and the stage of the cell cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of DNA replication in Drosophila and how this is altered in response to defects in DNA replication.
the mechanisms that ensure that DNA replication is restricted to a single round per cell cycle.
the regulation of the pre-Replicative complex at origins of replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Dup destruction and Gem inhibition of Dup are coupled to the initiation of DNA replication.
Dup destruction is coupled with DNA replication and that Gem protein balances the elevated levels of Dup to prevent reformation of the pre-Replicative complex when Dup is not properly degraded.
the levels of the origin-binding proteins Double parked and its antagonist Geminin increase when DNA replication is defective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the levels of Dup and Gem are regulated in response to DNA replication to prevent re-replicated chromosomes.
Dup is rapidly destroyed in response to DNA replication and this destruction prevents the re-formation of pre-RCs.
Dup is rapidly destroyed during G1-S, but when this fails to occur, Gem protein levels increase to prevent re-replicating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Dup is regulated in response to replication, not cell-cycle progression.
the levels of the origin-binding proteins, Dup and Gem, are coupled to replication and that this coupling may be a mechanism for preventing re-replication in cycling cells.
Dup is stabilized by defects in replication and that this stabilization of Dup is cell-type specific.
